outcome: Infant admission to the neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 2,497 pregnant patients who delivered at a single, large, Midwest academic medical center over 1 year.
finding: Distance to care, rather than rurality, was a key predictor of multiple adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm labor, pre-eclampsia, infant admission to the NICU, lower gestational age at delivery, and lower birth weight.
gest_age: Lower in patients living further from the medical center
birth_weight: Lower in infants of patients living further from the medical center
